items.detail: A connector's standalone service answers a typed descriptor and invokes its operations over HTTP; admission and freshness are checked before dispatch.
items.label: Describe and invoke

items.detail: connectors serve puts one gateway in front of several standalone services, prefixes their operations and reports a downstream failure without retrying it.
items.label: One-hop federation

items.detail: A host whose service configuration names a state directory serves POST /v1alpha2/invoke: every admitted invocation is anchored in the execution audit before dispatch (since 0.35.0).
items.label: Audited v1alpha2 invoke

items.detail: An admitted write records its attempt before its one dispatch and answers it as mutation; a lost answer is outcome_unknown and is never sent again (since 0.35.0).
items.label: The attempt a write produced

items.detail: connectors_client::Client::invoke_v1alpha2 returns the attempt the host recorded and reports an older host as unsupported instead of falling back.
items.label: Rust client for v1alpha2

items.detail: Principal, tenant, grant and delegated approval on the service wire are specified; the runtime implements only the first v1alpha2 invoke binding.
items.label: Governed service admission

items.detail: setup init creates a private configuration and an Entity Runtime metadata store over Eventlog SQLite, with durable open checkpoints (since 0.33.0).
items.label: Setup and metadata store

items.detail: A local owner starts the process that serves each configured instance, refuses a changed executable or configuration before provider work, and stops exact incarnations.
items.label: Supervised instances

items.detail: setup owner-stop asks the state directory's running owner, of any build, to drain and exit within 30 seconds, answers no_owner when none runs, and never signals a process.
items.label: Stopping an owner after an upgrade

items.detail: After a configuration change each saved connection has one working path: revalidate, a new connection under the same instance id after an evidence lifetime change, or a new instance id after a changed provider authority or profile.
items.label: Configuration upgrades

items.detail: approvals clock-check names why the quorum formed no answer (below quorum, split or too imprecise) with its next action, and each source's result: unreachable, unverified or verified at any radius; only the combined answer is capped.
items.label: Approval clock refusals

items.detail: connections connect validates a credential and keeps it in Secret Service custody; revalidate, reconnect and revoke manage it, and an unanswered revalidation is outcome_unknown.
items.label: Saved connections

items.detail: A connection connected or revalidated once keeps serving reads across any number of evidence lifetimes: a read on lapsed evidence recollects it once from custody, with no re-entry, before it is served.
items.label: Unattended reads

items.detail: A connectors-local/5 configuration enables connectors by name and names their instances; an instance that pins nothing is derived from the catalog provider installed beside the CLI.
items.label: Connector instances

items.detail: --connector and --instance select one instance; the deprecated --adapter reaches the same instance and says it is deprecated once.
items.label: Selecting an instance

items.detail: instances replaces the adapters group and connections reconnect replaces connections repair; each old name runs as its new one and says it is deprecated once.
items.label: Renamed commands

items.detail: A connection whose stored credential the provider refused is Stale until connections reconnect publishes a new credential under the same reference.
items.label: Stale connections

items.detail: connections connect is refused while the instance holds a published Live or Stale connection, naming the reconnect, revalidation or revocation that helps.
items.label: One connection per instance

items.detail: setup migrate moves each legacy catalog entry to an instance of its connector, keeping its instance id, revision, executable selection and custody items, and names why any other entry is kept.
items.label: Configuration migration

items.detail: An owner configuration can explicitly select read-only mounted-secret custody (mounted_secret, Linux): connect, list and a credentialed invoke run under an empty environment in a container, reading a Kubernetes-style Secret volume and writing nothing; rotation needs a revalidation.
items.label: Mounted-secret custody

items.detail: approvals policy-set, prepare and issue bind a write's whole input to a protected proof before the host dispatches it once.
items.label: Approved writes

items.detail: Approval-signing keys are initialized, rotated, recovered, revoked and retired through the CLI; status reads never touch custody.
items.label: Approval-signing keys

items.detail: approvals clock-check answers from a quorum of two to eight configured Roughtime sources, naming each source's result, without starting the owner or reading metadata.
items.label: Approval clock check

items.detail: connections launch hands one connection's protected document to a pinned consumer and refuses a launch its configuration does not admit (since 0.31.0).
items.label: Consumer launch

items.detail: operations list --family names the operations of one contract family, such as datasource.feed/v1alpha1, with their contract and profile.
items.label: Operations by family

items.detail: With --output json, invoke results and operation schemas are JSON values, not JSON text (breaking since 0.32.0).
items.label: JSON values in JSON answers

items.detail: connectors-build catalog compiles a pinned OpenAPI document into a digest-verified bundle; every committed bundle matches a fresh run byte for byte.
items.label: Bundles from pinned sources

items.detail: A selection's guard reads before the one request and refuses unless every check holds; after it, a failed check leaves the outcome uncertain, never refused.
items.label: Guarded writes as data

items.detail: Projects, issues, files, the repository tree, branches, tags, releases, commits, commit diffs, compares, code search, deployments, environments, pipelines, jobs, traces, merge requests and their diffs and discussions as reads; issue, merge-request (auto-merge and reopen included), note, discussion, tag and release writes under approval.
items.label: GitLab

items.detail: pipeline.retry, pipeline.cancel, pipeline.create, commit.create, file.update, branch.create, branch.delete and project.create under approval, each guarded on the caller's commit (project.create on the namespace path and id) and proven by GitLab's answer or a read after it; environments.list as a read; verified against fixtures, not a live GitLab.
items.label: GitLab CI, branch, commit and project writes

items.detail: GitLab binds datasource.feed/v1alpha1 as profile gitlab-merge-requests/1, checked against recorded GitLab answers (since 0.32.0).
items.label: GitLab merge-request feed

items.detail: Issue search by JQL, one issue by key, comments, changelogs, an issue's available transitions, a project's creatable issue types, user search, an attachment's content, and running one transition by id under a guard that reads the issue before and after it, over HTTP basic authentication (one issue, issue types and user search since 0.39.0).
items.label: Jira Cloud

items.detail: A selection can read an answer as bytes: media type, length, SHA-256 and the bytes in base64, at most 2 MiB and refused as capacity above it, with at most three redirects, each only to an origin the selection names and the connection admits in its hosts; verified against fixtures only.
items.label: Binary responses

items.detail: attachment.content reads one attachment as a binary body, directly with redirect=false or through Jira's 303 to an admitted media host; that host, api.media.atlassian.com, is inferred and not verified against a live site.
items.label: Jira attachment content

items.detail: Changed pages, a space's pages, one page with its body and a page's comments; exercised against local fixtures only.
items.label: Confluence Cloud

items.detail: CQL search, changed pages by CQL, spaces, one space, a space's content, one page with its body and a page's comments under the provider id confluence-v1, from a source document this repository writes from Atlassian's v1 reference; exercised against local fixtures only.
items.label: Confluence Cloud REST v1

items.detail: One object type's records, paged, and one record by id; exercised against local fixtures only.
items.label: HubSpot CRM

items.detail: Tickets, users and organizations changed since a start time, one of each by id, and a ticket's comments, with OAuth client credentials or an API token; a ticket update, a private note and a draft reply behind an approval, refused as a conflict when the ticket changed since it was read.
items.label: Zendesk Support

items.detail: Reads and guarded writes from Discovery documents projected to OpenAPI, with a refresh token from browser consent; exercised against local fixtures only.
items.label: Google Drive, Slides, Calendar and Gmail

items.detail: pod.create, pods.list and pod.terminate with the API key in custody; a create without a definite answer is unknown and never sent again, and one refused for lack of capacity is refused as capacity; verified against a local fixture only (since 0.36.0).
items.label: Runpod pods

items.detail: A Swagger 2.0 document is ingested through an exact, recorded projection to OpenAPI 3.1.0; a construct without an exact row is refused by name (since 0.37.0).
items.label: Swagger 2.0 sources

items.detail: conversations.list, conversations.history and conversations.replies with a bot token (since 0.38.0), users.list, team.info, emoji.list and auth.test, and on a second connection with a user token search.messages and the three conversation reads and users.list, which reach every conversation that user can read, the channels the bot is not in included; verified against a local fixture only.
items.label: Slack conversations

items.detail: chat.postMessage posts a message, a thread reply included, conversations.open opens a direct message to post to, and chat.update and chat.delete edit and delete a message the bot posted, each under approval after the token's auth.test read; an edit or delete Slack refuses by name (cant_update_message, cant_delete_message, message_not_found) is refused, and a dispatch without a definite answer, or any other 200 with ok false, is unknown; none is sent again; verified against a local fixture only.
items.label: Slack messages

items.detail: files.list, files.info and file.download, which reads a file's url_private on files.slack.com as a binary body with the bot token, only where the connection admits that host with the credential; verified against a local fixture only.
items.label: Slack files

items.detail: A Slack read answered 200 with ok false is refused, never returned as an empty read: Slack's error is the reason, and missing_scope and not_in_channel are forbidden, invalid_auth and its kin unauthorized, an unknown channel, thread, file or user not_found, ratelimited rate_limited with its Retry-After, a bad cursor or argument invalid_input, and any other name internal, on every JSON read of both Slack sets; verified against a local fixture only.
items.label: Slack read refusals

items.detail: alerts.list and incidents.list over a creation window the caller advances, alert.get, incident.get and incident.alert_ids, read only, with the key sent as GenieKey <key>; verified against a local fixture only.
items.label: Opsgenie alerts and incidents

items.detail: Listing and locating precompiled bundles with provenance is specified; directly configured adapters need no index.
items.label: Catalog index service

items.detail: resources.list, endpoints.discover and optionally hosts.discover, scoped to configured namespaces and kinds, with a saved bearer token.
items.label: Kubernetes reads and discovery

items.detail: resources.get reads one object by name, namespaces.list the configured namespaces the cluster has, deployments.history the ReplicaSets a Deployment controls; replicasets and events are configurable kinds; verified against API-shaped fixtures.
items.label: Kubernetes single objects, namespaces and rollout history

items.detail: statefulsets is a configurable kind; nodes.list pages the full Node objects when node_reads is configured; custom_resources.list pages one configured namespaced custom resource collection by group, version and plural; verified against API-shaped fixtures.
items.label: Kubernetes statefulsets, nodes and custom resources

items.detail: A kubeconfig user that authenticates through an exec plugin, such as aws eks get-token, is reached when the local configuration pins the plugin by absolute path and sha256: it runs on Linux from the descriptor it was hashed through, with the kubeconfig arguments, an empty environment plus an allow-list, a deadline and an output bound, and its token is held in memory until expiry; verified with fixture plugins against a recorded API session, not a live EKS cluster.
items.label: Kubernetes exec credential plugin

items.detail: pods.logs reads a bounded tail of one container's log in a configured namespace, at most 1,000 lines and 128 KiB, when pod_logs is configured; verified against API-shaped fixtures.
items.label: Kubernetes pod logs

items.detail: contexts.list lists the contexts of the one kubeconfig a local configuration names, never its credentials or servers, with no cluster request.
items.label: Kubernetes kubeconfig contexts

items.detail: pods.exec runs one command as an argument vector in a named container, through the local CLI under approval, when pod_exec is configured; exit status and bounded output come back, and a lost stream is unknown and never resent; verified against recorded streams, not a live cluster.
items.label: Kubernetes pod exec

items.detail: History, status, values and manifest of a named release, values and manifests disclosed only as redacted projections.
items.label: Helm release reads

items.detail: schema.list, query.read, database.list, table.list, table.describe and index.list in a read-only transaction with fixed statement and lock timeouts; a deadline or a dropped invocation cancels the query.
items.label: PostgreSQL reads

items.detail: The same six reads on a connection whose engine is mysql, in a read-only session bound to the configured database, over TLS unless plaintext is allowed.
items.label: MySQL reads

items.detail: profile.read runs a read the operator declares in the native file by name, on either engine: declared parameters only, bound; typed columns with numbers masked by default; one call identifier; keyset pages that never take a short page for the end and refuse, rather than skip, a non-unique ordering value at a page boundary; cursors checked for shape, type and context; verified against scripted wire fixtures, not a live database.
items.label: SQL read profiles

items.detail: websearch.search, websearch.fetch and websearch.crawl through the shared websearch family; the key is checked without spending a search.
items.label: Tavily web search

items.detail: logs.query_range, logs.query_metric and logs.labels through a saved bearer connection (since 0.38.0).
items.label: Loki LogQL reads

items.detail: logs.profile_lines (one typed, masked record per line of a configured line profile) and logs.call_trace (one call's lines from every source, by its identifier) through a saved bearer connection.
items.label: Loki line and trace profiles

items.detail: A configured SQL read profile over the call table and a configured Loki line profile over the CDR lines, joined by a workflow on the call identifier each declares, answer every leg of a transferred call with its type, numbers masked, across a page boundary of the SQL read.
items.label: A call by its number, every leg typed

items.detail: datasources.list through a saved service-account connection, and Loki reads through Grafana's data-source proxy (since 0.39.0).
items.label: Grafana data sources

items.detail: irm.alert_groups.list, irm.alert_group.get, irm.incidents.list and irm.incident.get over a since window, with incident-to-alert-group links (inferred), through a saved IRM service-account connection; read only.
items.label: Grafana IRM alert groups and incidents

items.detail: series.query, series.query_range and rules.list through a saved bearer connection, directly or through Grafana's data-source proxy.
items.label: Prometheus PromQL reads

items.detail: Per-operation SelfSubjectAccessReview checks and the remaining Kubernetes and Helm workflows.
items.label: Kubernetes permission checks

items.detail: An X-Scope-OrgID tenant header and profiles other than a bearer token; today a Loki without authentication cannot be connected.
items.label: Loki tenants and other authentication

items.detail: An X-Scope-OrgID tenant header, an adapter-set query timeout, a Capacity error for too many samples apart from other execution errors, and profiles other than a bearer token.
items.label: Prometheus tenants, timeouts and other authentication

items.detail: Atlassian native documents, Docker, Alertmanager, SIP and RTVBP have designs or typed models and no runtime; Grafana dashboards, datasource discovery and the mediated route are specified and not built.
items.label: Specification-only adapters

items.detail: MCP invocation, projection, auth lifecycle, mutation replay and composition contracts are specified; there is no MCP runtime.
items.label: MCP

items.detail: A release page carries an archive per Linux and macOS target (x86_64 and aarch64) holding connectors and connectors-catalog-provider, with SHA256SUMS; the other adapters are built from the checkout, and there is no Windows binary.
items.label: Release binaries

items.detail: No package manager, container registry or Windows binary carries a release.
items.label: Package distribution

source: connectors-docs, from its capability list; every shipped item names the test that holds it
